model_given.instructions: TRUDI SIFT MCP Server — exposes SANS SIFT Workstation forensic tools as typed MCP tools. All tools are read-only with respect to evidence. Output paths must be within analysis/, exports/, or reports/ directories. Timestamps are always UTC.

tools.name: img_vshadow_mount
tools.title: Img Vshadow Mount
tools.description:
Mount Volume Shadow Copies (VSS) from a disk image or device using vshadowmount.
Exposes shadow copies as vss1, vss2, ... under mount_point (libvshadow 2024
naming; the returned `shadow_paths` list gives the exact paths). Each shadow
copy is a raw NTFS volume image: run tsk.fls / tsk.icat directly on it, or
mount it read-only with mount_ntfs().

offset: byte offset of the NTFS VOLUME inside a whole-disk image
        (partition start sector x sector size — the same offset used
        to mount the volume itself, e.g. 105906176 for a 2048-sector
        start at 512 B/sector). REQUIRED for a full-disk E01/raw
        image: without it vshadowmount is pointed at the MBR, finds no
        VSS store, and exposes an EMPTY directory that looks mounted.
        Leave 0 for a bare volume image or a partition device.
allow_other: pass -X allow_other so the unprivileged MCP process (and
        tsk.fls / fsstat run without sudo) can read the FUSE mount.
        Without it every follow-up call gets "Permission denied".

The store is probed with vshadowinfo first; if none is found at this
offset the call FAILS (with an offset hint) instead of leaving a silent
empty mount behind.

tools.name: img_vshadow_list
tools.title: Img Vshadow List
tools.description:
List mounted Volume Shadow Copies after vshadow_mount.
Shows available vss1, vss2, etc. entries (each a raw NTFS volume image).

tools.name: img_vshadow_umount
tools.title: Img Vshadow Umount
tools.description: Unmount a vshadowmount mount point.

tools.name: img_bde_mount
tools.title: Img Bde Mount
tools.description:
Mount a BitLocker-encrypted image or partition using bdemount.
Provide either recovery_password (48-digit key) or recovery_key_file path.
After mounting, run mount_ntfs() on mount_point/bde1 with offset=0.

tools.name: img_bde_info
tools.title: Img Bde Info
tools.description: Display BitLocker encryption information from an image.

tools.name: img_xmount_image
tools.title: Img Xmount Image
tools.description:
Mount a disk image in any format as a raw device using xmount.
input_format: 'ewf' (E01), 'aff', 'vmdk', 'vhd', 'vdi', 'raw', 'dmg'.
output_format: 'raw' (default) — exposes as /mount_point/<image>.dd.
Useful when a tool doesn't support E01 natively (pass the raw file instead).

tools.name: img_xmount_umount
tools.title: Img Xmount Umount
tools.description: Unmount an xmount mount point.

tools.name: img_photorec_carve
tools.title: Img Photorec Carve
tools.description:
Carve files from a disk image by file signature using PhotoRec (non-interactive mode).
output_dir: destination directory for recovered files.
file_types: comma-separated type extensions to recover e.g. 'jpg,pdf,doc,zip'.
partition: partition number to scan (0 = whole disk, default).

Note: PhotoRec creates numbered subdirectories (recup_dir.1, recup_dir.2, ...) inside output_dir.
For large images this can take hours and recover thousands of files.

tools.name: img_partprobe_refresh
tools.title: Img Partprobe Refresh
tools.description: Inform the OS of partition table changes on a device.

tools.name: img_losetup_create
tools.title: Img Losetup Create
tools.description:
Create a loop device from a disk image (alternative to mount -o loop).
Returns the loop device path (e.g. /dev/loop0).

tools.name: img_losetup_list
tools.title: Img Losetup List
tools.description: List all active loop devices.

tools.name: img_losetup_detach
tools.title: Img Losetup Detach
tools.description: Detach a loop device (e.g. /dev/loop0).

tools.name: vol_info
tools.title: Vol Info
tools.description: Display OS version, architecture, and kernel build from a memory image.

tools.name: vol_symbol_check
tools.title: Vol Symbol Check
tools.description:
Pre-flight check: verify the memory image exists and Volatility 3 symbol
files are cached. Returns the resolved absolute path in the 'image' field
so downstream plugins can use it directly without re-expanding ~.

If symbols_ready is False, call vol_info once (requires internet) to
trigger the download for this kernel build, then retry memory plugins.

tools.name: vol_pslist
tools.title: Vol Pslist
tools.description: List processes via EPROCESS linked list walk. Fast; misses hidden processes.

tools.name: vol_psscan
tools.title: Vol Psscan
tools.description: Scan for EPROCESS pool tags — finds hidden and exited processes. Preferred over pslist.

tools.name: vol_pstree
tools.title: Vol Pstree
tools.description: Display process hierarchy with parent-child relationships.

tools.name: vol_psxview
tools.title: Vol Psxview
tools.description: Cross-reference process lists (pslist, psscan, sessions, etc.) to find hidden processes.

tools.name: vol_cmdline
tools.title: Vol Cmdline
tools.description: Extract command-line arguments for all or a specific process.

tools.name: vol_envars
tools.title: Vol Envars
tools.description: Extract environment variables per process (reveals working dir, injected vars).

tools.name: vol_getsids
tools.title: Vol Getsids
tools.description: Extract security identifiers (SIDs) associated with processes.

tools.name: vol_privileges
tools.title: Vol Privileges
tools.description: List token privileges per process (look for SeDebugPrivilege, SeTcbPrivilege).

tools.name: vol_dlllist
tools.title: Vol Dlllist
tools.description: List loaded DLLs per process. Check for spoofed or injected DLLs.

tools.name: vol_handles
tools.title: Vol Handles
tools.description:
List open handles per process (files, registry keys, mutexes, events, threads).

Volatility 3's `windows.handles` plugin only accepts --pid and --offset —
there is no built-in handle-type filter. To filter the result by type
(File, Key, Mutant, Thread, Process, Section, Event, …), grep the rendered
output column "Type" via `strings.grep` on the JSON output or pipe
the result through a downstream filter.

tools.name: vol_ldrmodules
tools.title: Vol Ldrmodules
tools.description: Cross-reference loaded modules across PEB/VAD/LDR lists. Discrepancies = injection indicator.

tools.name: vol_sessions
tools.title: Vol Sessions
tools.description: List active user sessions.

tools.name: vol_netstat
tools.title: Vol Netstat
tools.description: Walk TCP/IP structures — active connections at capture time.

tools.name: vol_netscan
tools.title: Vol Netscan
tools.description: Pool-tag scan for network connections — finds historical/closed connections too.

tools.name: vol_svcscan
tools.title: Vol Svcscan
tools.description: Enumerate services via pool scan — finds hidden and deleted services still in memory.

tools.name: vol_svclist
tools.title: Vol Svclist
tools.description: List services via SCM (Service Control Manager) structures.

tools.name: vol_svcdiff
tools.title: Vol Svcdiff
tools.description: Diff services found via SCM vs pool scan to detect hidden services.

tools.name: vol_registry_hivelist
tools.title: Vol Registry Hivelist
tools.description: List all loaded registry hives and their virtual addresses.

tools.name: vol_registry_hivescan
tools.title: Vol Registry Hivescan
tools.description: Pool-tag scan for registry hives — finds unloaded/hidden hives.

tools.name: vol_registry_printkey
tools.title: Vol Registry Printkey
tools.description:
Print a registry key and its values from memory.
key: e.g. 'SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'

tools.name: vol_userassist
tools.title: Vol Userassist
tools.description: Extract UserAssist registry entries — GUI execution evidence (programs run via Explorer).

tools.name: vol_registry_amcache
tools.title: Vol Registry Amcache
tools.description: Extract Amcache entries from memory (program execution evidence).

tools.name: vol_scheduled_tasks
tools.title: Vol Scheduled Tasks
tools.description: Extract scheduled tasks from registry in memory.

tools.name: vol_malfind
tools.title: Vol Malfind
tools.description:
Find RWX memory regions with PE headers or shellcode — primary injection scanner.
Set dump=True with output_dir to extract suspicious regions to disk.

tools.name: vol_vadinfo
tools.title: Vol Vadinfo
tools.description: Inspect Virtual Address Descriptor tree for a process — all memory regions.

tools.name: vol_vadwalk
tools.title: Vol Vadwalk
tools.description: Walk the VAD tree structure for a process.

tools.name: vol_hollowprocesses
tools.title: Vol Hollowprocesses
tools.description: Detect process hollowing by comparing VAD entries against PEB module list.

tools.name: vol_pebmasquerade
tools.title: Vol Pebmasquerade
tools.description: Detect PEB masquerading — process pretending to be a different executable.

tools.name: vol_suspicious_threads
tools.title: Vol Suspicious Threads
tools.description: Find threads with suspicious start addresses (e.g. starting in non-image memory).

tools.name: vol_vadyarascan
tools.title: Vol Vadyarascan
tools.description:
YARA scan of process VAD regions directly from memory.
yara_rules: path to a .yar file or inline rule string.

tools.name: vol_cmdscanner
tools.title: Vol Cmdscanner
tools.description: Scan for COMMAND_HISTORY and CONSOLE_INFORMATION structures — console input history.

tools.name: vol_consoles
tools.title: Vol Consoles
tools.description: Extract console I/O buffers — what was typed and displayed in cmd.exe windows.

tools.name: vol_modules
tools.title: Vol Modules
tools.description: List loaded kernel modules via linked list walk.

tools.name: vol_modscan
tools.title: Vol Modscan
tools.description: Pool-tag scan for kernel modules — finds hidden/unlinked drivers.

tools.name: vol_driverscan
tools.title: Vol Driverscan
tools.description: Scan for DRIVER_OBJECT structures in pool memory.

tools.name: vol_driverirp
tools.title: Vol Driverirp
tools.description: List IRP handlers for all drivers — used to find hooked dispatch routines.

tools.name: vol_devicetree
tools.title: Vol Devicetree
tools.description: Display driver/device object tree — shows device stacking for rootkit detection.

tools.name: vol_callbacks
tools.title: Vol Callbacks
tools.description: List kernel notification callbacks (PsSetCreateProcessNotifyRoutine, etc.).

tools.name: vol_ssdt
tools.title: Vol Ssdt
tools.description: Display the System Service Descriptor Table — detect SSDT hooks.

tools.name: vol_unhooked_system_calls
tools.title: Vol Unhooked System Calls
tools.description: Compare SSDT entries to expected values to find unhooked system calls.

tools.name: vol_filescan
tools.title: Vol Filescan
tools.description: Scan for FILE_OBJECT structures — lists all files cached in memory.

tools.name: vol_dumpfiles
tools.title: Vol Dumpfiles
tools.description:
Dump files from memory by virtual address (from filescan output) or PID.
Requires output_dir.

tools.name: vol_mftscan
tools.title: Vol Mftscan
tools.description: Scan for MFT entries in memory — finds files not in the live filesystem.

tools.name: vol_memmap
tools.title: Vol Memmap
tools.description:
Show or dump memory map for a process.
Set dump=True with output_dir to write process memory to disk.

tools.name: vol_amcache
tools.title: Vol Amcache
tools.description: Extract Amcache.hve entries from a running system — program execution evidence.

tools.name: vol_shimcachemem
tools.title: Vol Shimcachemem
tools.description: Extract AppCompatCache (ShimCache) from memory — execution evidence with timestamps.

tools.name: vol_hashdump
tools.title: Vol Hashdump
tools.description: Dump NTLM password hashes from SAM and SYSTEM hives in memory.

tools.name: vol_cachedump
tools.title: Vol Cachedump
tools.description: Extract cached domain credentials (DCC2 hashes) from memory.

tools.name: vol_lsadump
tools.title: Vol Lsadump
tools.description: Dump LSA secrets from memory (service account passwords, auto-logon creds).

tools.name: vol_mutantscan
tools.title: Vol Mutantscan
tools.description: Scan for mutex objects — malware often uses mutexes to prevent reinfection.

tools.name: vol_symlinkscan
tools.title: Vol Symlinkscan
tools.description: Scan for symbolic link objects in kernel pool memory.

tools.name: vol_thrdscan
tools.title: Vol Thrdscan
tools.description: Scan for ETHREAD objects — thread-level investigation.

tools.name: vol_timeliner
tools.title: Vol Timeliner
tools.description:
Generate a unified timeline of all memory artifacts.
Produces a bodyfile suitable for mactime.

tools.name: vol_yarascan
tools.title: Vol Yarascan
tools.description: YARA scan across all process memory regions.

tools.name: vol_linux_pslist
tools.title: Vol Linux Pslist
tools.description: List Linux processes.

tools.name: vol_linux_psscan
tools.title: Vol Linux Psscan
tools.description: Scan for Linux TASK_STRUCT objects.

tools.name: vol_linux_pstree
tools.title: Vol Linux Pstree
tools.description: Linux process hierarchy.

tools.name: vol_linux_netstat
tools.title: Vol Linux Netstat
tools.description: Linux network connections from memory.

tools.name: vol_linux_lsof
tools.title: Vol Linux Lsof
tools.description: List open files per Linux process.

tools.name: vol_linux_malfind
tools.title: Vol Linux Malfind
tools.description: Find suspicious memory regions in Linux processes.

tools.name: vol_linux_lsmod
tools.title: Vol Linux Lsmod
tools.description: List loaded Linux kernel modules.

tools.name: vol_linux_check_modules
tools.title: Vol Linux Check Modules
tools.description: Detect hidden kernel modules on Linux — compares sysfs vs module list.

tools.name: tsk_mmls
tools.title: Tsk Mmls
tools.description: Display partition table (MBR and GPT) — get sector offsets for mounting.

tools.name: tsk_fsstat
tools.title: Tsk Fsstat
tools.description:
Filesystem metadata: NTFS version, cluster size, MFT offset, volume ID.
offset_sectors: sector offset from mmls output (required for partitioned images).

tools.name: tsk_fls
tools.title: Tsk Fls
tools.description:
List files and directories in a disk image, including deleted entries (marked *).
offset_sectors: from mmls output.
inode: list a specific directory by inode number.
recursive: recurse into subdirectories.
bodyfile: output in mactime bodyfile format for timeline creation.
deleted_only: show only deleted entries.

tools.name: tsk_istat
tools.title: Tsk Istat
tools.description:
Display inode metadata: MAC times, size, allocated blocks, file type.
offset_sectors: from mmls output.

tools.name: tsk_icat
tools.title: Tsk Icat
tools.description:
Extract file content by inode number to output_path.
inode: can be a number or 'number-stream-id' for ADS (e.g. '11-128-4').
recover_deleted: attempt recovery of deleted file data.
slack_space: extract file slack space.

tools.name: tsk_ils
tools.title: Tsk Ils
tools.description:
List inodes in a filesystem.
orphan_only: unlinked inodes (deleted files with no directory entry).
unallocated_only: only unallocated inodes.
allocated_only: only allocated inodes.

tools.name: tsk_ffind
tools.title: Tsk Ffind
tools.description: Find the filename(s) for a given inode number.

tools.name: tsk_blkls
tools.title: Tsk Blkls
tools.description:
Extract raw disk blocks for carving.
unallocated_only: extract only unallocated blocks (default — for carving).
output_path: destination file for raw block data.

tools.name: tsk_recover
tools.title: Tsk Recover
tools.description:
Bulk extract files from a disk image.
include_unallocated: also recover deleted/unallocated files.

tools.name: tsk_mactime
tools.title: Tsk Mactime
tools.description:
Generate a MAC timeline from a bodyfile (output of fls -m).
start_date / end_date: filter to a date range, format YYYY-MM-DD.
csv_output: produce comma-separated output (easier for analysis).

tools.name: tsk_blkcat
tools.title: Tsk Blkcat
tools.description: Extract raw content of a specific data block.

tools.name: tsk_blkstat
tools.title: Tsk Blkstat
tools.description: Display statistics on a specific data block (allocation status, containing file).

tools.name: tsk_blkcalc
tools.title: Tsk Blkcalc
tools.description: Convert between disk and image block addresses.

tools.name: tsk_mmcat
tools.title: Tsk Mmcat
tools.description: Output the contents of a partition slot (raw partition data).

tools.name: tsk_mmstat
tools.title: Tsk Mmstat
tools.description: Display statistics about the volume system (disk layout metadata).

tools.name: tsk_hfind
tools.title: Tsk Hfind
tools.description:
Look up a file hash in a hash database (NSRL, hashkeeper, md5sum format).
hash_db: path to the hash database file.
hash_value: the hash to look up.
lookup_type: 'md5', 'sha1', 'nsrl-md5', 'nsrl-sha1'.

tools.name: tsk_sigfind
tools.title: Tsk Sigfind
tools.description:
Find a hex byte signature in a disk image.
signature_hex: hex string to search for e.g. 'MZ' header = '4D5A'.
Useful for locating hidden PE files or deleted MBR signatures.

tools.name: tsk_sorter
tools.title: Tsk Sorter
tools.description:
Sort files from a disk image into categories based on file type.
output_dir: destination for sorted file categories.
category: limit to a specific category e.g. 'images', 'exec', 'audio', 'documents'.

tools.name: tsk_jls
tools.title: Tsk Jls
tools.description:
List journal entries from an ext3/ext4 filesystem.
Useful for recovering deleted files on Linux disk images.

tools.name: tsk_jcat
tools.title: Tsk Jcat
tools.description:
Output the contents of an ext3/ext4 journal entry by inode number.
Use after tsk_jls to inspect a specific journal block.

tools.name: tsk_indxparse
tools.title: Tsk Indxparse
tools.description:
Parse NTFS $INDX records (directory index slack) using INDXParse.py.
Recovers deleted directory entries that MFTECmd and Vol3 miss.

mft_path: path to the $MFT file (or any file containing $INDX records).
output_path: optional output destination (analysis/exports/reports).

tools.name: ewf_mount_ntfs
tools.title: Ewf Mount Ntfs
tools.description:
Mount an NTFS partition from a raw EWF device.
offset_bytes: byte offset = sector_start * sector_size (from mmls output).
Always mounts read-only, with norecover to prevent NTFS journal replay.
Falls back to an explicit ntfs-3g filesystem type when the kernel has no
in-built NTFS driver.

tools.name: ewf_umount_filesystem
tools.title: Ewf Umount Filesystem
tools.description: Unmount a mounted filesystem.

tools.name: ewf_mount_full_image
tools.title: Ewf Mount Full Image
tools.description:
Convenience: mount an E01 image end-to-end.
1. ewfmount the E01 to ewf_mount_point (exposes ewf1)
2. Read partition table via mmls
3. Probe candidate partitions with fsstat and mount the NTFS one

Returns the mount result and the detected NTFS offset in bytes.

tools.name: ewf_info
tools.title: Ewf Info
tools.description: Display E01 image metadata: acquisition hash, timestamps, notes, examiner info.

tools.name: ewf_verify
tools.title: Ewf Verify
tools.description:
Verify E01 image integrity by recomputing and comparing MD5/SHA1 hashes.
Must complete without errors before analysis proceeds.

tools.name: ewf_mount
tools.title: Ewf Mount
tools.description:
Mount an E01/EWF image as a raw device at mount_point.
For multi-segment images (E01/E02/...) specify the first segment only.
After mounting, run tsk_mmls against mount_point/ewf1 to get partition offsets.

tools.name: ewf_umount
tools.title: Ewf Umount
tools.description: Unmount an EWF mount point.

tools.name: ez_mftecmd
tools.title: Ez Mftecmd
tools.description:
Parse the Master File Table ($MFT) from a mounted or extracted NTFS volume.
mft_path: path to $MFT file (e.g. /mnt/windows_mount/$MFT or extracted copy).
Produces CSV with all file metadata, timestamps, and attributes.

tools.name: ez_mftecmd_dir
tools.title: Ez Mftecmd Dir
tools.description: Parse $MFT from a directory scan of a mounted volume (searches for $MFT automatically).

tools.name: ez_evtxecmd
tools.title: Ez Evtxecmd
tools.description:
Parse Windows Event Log (.evtx) files with enriched field mapping.
evtx_path: path to a single .evtx file or a directory of .evtx files.
event_ids: comma-separated event IDs to filter (e.g. '4624,4625,4688').
Maps decode raw XML fields into human-readable columns.

tools.name: ez_recmd_hive
tools.title: Ez Recmd Hive
tools.description:
Parse a single registry hive using a RECmd batch file.
hive_path: path to SYSTEM, SOFTWARE, SAM, SECURITY, NTUSER.DAT, etc.
batch_file: path to .reb batch file (defaults to DFIRBatch.reb)

tools.name: ez_recmd_dir
tools.title: Ez Recmd Dir
tools.description: Parse all registry hives in a directory recursively using a RECmd batch file.

tools.name: ez_recmd_batch
tools.title: Ez Recmd Batch
tools.description:
Run a RECmd batch config (targeted key extraction) over the hives under
`hives_dir`.

per_hive=True (default): enumerate the hive FILES (NTUSER.DAT, UsrClass.dat,
SAM, SYSTEM, SOFTWARE, SECURITY, Amcache.hve) under the tree and run RECmd
`-f <hive> --bn <batch>` per hive, each with the normal timeout, output under
`<output_dir>/<profile-or-parent>/`. One traced, citable call per hive;
failures are isolated. `-d <whole tree>` is what ran to the 1800 s timeout
twice on a full Users tree — kept behind per_hive=False for small dirs.

tools.name: ez_amcacheparser
tools.title: Ez Amcacheparser
tools.description:
Parse Amcache.hve — program execution evidence with SHA1 hashes.
amcache_path: path to Amcache.hve (usually Windows/AppCompat/Programs/Amcache.hve).

tools.name: ez_appcompatcacheparser
tools.title: Ez Appcompatcacheparser
tools.description:
Parse AppCompatCache (ShimCache) from SYSTEM hive — execution evidence with timestamps.
system_hive: path to SYSTEM registry hive.

tools.name: ez_pecmd
tools.title: Ez Pecmd
tools.description:
Parse Windows Prefetch files — execution timestamps (up to 8 last run times), file references.
prefetch_path: path to a single .pf file or the Prefetch directory.

Off Windows PECmd cannot decompress; libscca writes the same CSV (`parser`).

tools.name: ez_jlecmd
tools.title: Ez Jlecmd
tools.description:
Parse Jump Lists (AutomaticDestinations / CustomDestinations).
jump_list_path: path to a single .automaticDestinations-ms file or directory.

tools.name: ez_lecmd
tools.title: Ez Lecmd
tools.description:
Parse Windows shortcut (.lnk) files — reveal accessed paths, timestamps, machine info.
lnk_path: path to a single .lnk file or a directory to scan recursively.

tools.name: ez_sbecmd
tools.title: Ez Sbecmd
tools.description:
Parse Shellbags (UsrClass.dat) — folder access history including network and removable media.
usrclass_path: path to UsrClass.dat hive.

tools.name: ez_rbcmd
tools.title: Ez Rbcmd
tools.description:
Parse Recycle Bin $I files — deleted file metadata (original path, deletion time, file size).
recycle_bin_path: path to $Recycle.Bin directory or a single $I file.

tools.name: ez_wxtcmd
tools.title: Ez Wxtcmd
tools.description:
Parse Windows 10 Timeline database (ActivitiesCache.db) — user activity history.
timeline_db: path to ActivitiesCache.db.

tools.name: ez_sqlecmd
tools.title: Ez Sqlecmd
tools.description:
Parse SQLite databases with known schema maps (browser history, Windows Timeline, etc.).
db_path: path to a single .db file or directory to scan.
output_file: ignored (SQLECmd writes one CSV per matched map).

tools.name: ez_bstrings
tools.title: Ez Bstrings
tools.description:
Extract strings from binary files with better filtering than GNU strings.
target_path: file or directory to scan.
min_length: minimum string length.
pattern: optional regex pattern to filter results.

tools.name: ez_rla
tools.title: Ez Rla
tools.description:
Replay registry transaction logs against hives for complete, up-to-date data.
hive_dir: directory containing hive files and their .LOG1/.LOG2 files.

tools.name: ez_recentfilecache
tools.title: Ez Recentfilecache
tools.description:
Parse RecentFileCache.bcf — Windows XP/Vista execution artifact.
rfc_path: path to RecentFileCache.bcf.

tools.name: plaso_create_timeline
tools.title: Plaso Create Timeline
tools.description:
Create a Plaso storage file from an evidence source (disk image, directory, or file).
evidence_path: E01 image, mounted directory, memory image, or log file.
storage_file: output .plaso file path (must be in analysis/ or exports/).
parsers: comma-separated parser names to limit scope (omit for all parsers).
Note: Full disk images take 1-6 hours depending on size. Use filters to scope.

tools.name: plaso_create_targeted
tools.title: Plaso Create Targeted
tools.description:
Create a targeted Plaso timeline using artifact filters (much faster than full parse).
artifact_filters: comma-separated artifact names e.g.
    'WindowsEventLogs,WindowsPrefetch,WindowsRegistryCurrentUser,WindowsMFT'
Common artifacts: WindowsEventLogs, WindowsPrefetch, WindowsRegistryCurrentUser,
    WindowsRegistryCurrentControlSet, WindowsMFT, WindowsRecycleBin,
    WindowsScheduledTasks, WindowsUserShellFolders

tools.name: plaso_export_csv
tools.title: Plaso Export Csv
tools.description:
Export a Plaso storage file to l2tCSV format.
time_filter: e.g. "date > '2023-01-20' AND date < '2023-01-30'"
query_filter: additional psort query filter expression.

tools.name: plaso_export_json
tools.title: Plaso Export Json
tools.description: Export a Plaso storage file to JSON Lines format.

tools.name: plaso_info
tools.title: Plaso Info
tools.description: Display metadata and statistics about a Plaso storage file (event counts, parsers used).

tools.name: plaso_filter_incident_window
tools.title: Plaso Filter Incident Window
tools.description:
Export events within an incident time window to CSV.
start_utc / end_utc: ISO format e.g. '2023-01-24 00:00:00'

tools.name: plaso_list_parsers
tools.title: Plaso List Parsers
tools.description: List all available Plaso parsers and plugins.

tools.name: yara_scan_file
tools.title: Yara Scan File
tools.description:
Scan a single file with YARA rules.
rules_path: path to a .yar file or a directory of .yar/.yara files.
Returns all matching rules with offsets and string identifiers.

tools.name: yara_scan_directory
tools.title: Yara Scan Directory
tools.description:
Scan all files in a directory with YARA rules.
Returns files with matches only (non-matching files omitted).

tools.name: yara_scan_process_memory

tools.name: strings_grep
tools.title: Strings Grep
tools.description:
Extract strings from a file and filter by regex pattern, STREAMING.
Useful for targeted IOC hunting: URLs, IPs, domain names, commands.
encoding: "ascii" (default), "utf16le" (Windows wide strings), or "both".

The whole `strings` stream is filtered line by line, so the result is a
true answer over the ENTIRE file. Contract:
  match_count   total matching lines in the file (counted past the cap)
  matches       the first `max_matches` of them
  complete      True when the whole file was scanned
  truncated     True when `matches` was capped OR the scan did not
                complete — a negative is only trustworthy when
                match_count == 0 and complete is True and truncated is
                False (the negative_from_truncated gate reads this).

Why streaming: buffering the whole `strings` output through the executor's
stdout cap (~50 KB) before the regex would silently drop any match beyond
the cap and report match_count 0 with success:true — a false negative with
no truncation signal, which reads as "the string is absent" when it is
present past the cap.

tools.name: net_http_session_inventory
tools.title: Net Http Session Inventory
tools.description:
Structured extraction of every HTTP session identity artifact from a PCAP.
Returns a deterministic table — prefer this over keyword `ngrep` searches

      Hotmail MSPAuth, AOL a/b, Facebook c_user/login_x, etc.)
    - URL auth parameters from GET/POST request lines
      (login=, email=, user=, gausr=, account=, screenname=, sn=)
    - Authorization headers
    - Email-like strings in URL paths/queries

Output is a structured dict rather than raw text — no keyword guessing,
no missed fields. Use this as the first identity-extraction step on any
PCAP investigation; only fall back to ngrep for ad-hoc keyword lookups.

structured table as JSON.

profile/login fields, then cross-references them against roster-derived

traffic, especially when multiple accounts appear on the same source host.

output_path: optional JSON path under analysis/ or exports/.

tools.description:

libevt's `evtexport`, because python-evtx parses only the binary-XML
EVTX format and, handed an EVT file, exits 0 with an empty <Events/>
document — a silent false negative that makes an XP-era event log look
empty. The result carries `log_format` so the caller knows which parser
produced it.

tools.name: misc_evtx_filter
tools.title: Misc Evtx Filter
tools.description:
Stream-filter an EVTX for specific event IDs without buffering the
entire XML dump in memory.

Buffering the whole evtx_dump.py XML output before filtering can expand a
large Security.evtx to hundreds of MB and blow both memory and the client
tool-timeout. This pipes evtx_dump.py through a line-by-line state machine
that keeps only the current Event in a small buffer and accumulates matches
as it goes.

event_ids: comma-separated event IDs e.g. '4624,4625,4688,4698'.
max_results: stop streaming after this many matches (default 200).
wall_clock_budget_s: kill the stream after this many seconds so the
                     MCP client doesn't time us out from the outside
                     (default 60).

tools.name: misc_chat_db_export
tools.title: Misc Chat Db Export
tools.description:
Export a chat/messenger sqlite store (Skype main.db, WhatsApp
msgstore.db) to normalized CSVs — the comms channel the mail extractors
(readpst/pff_export) do not cover, and a first-class exfil channel
(message bodies AND the Transfers file-transfer trail).

ENUMERATE, DON'T SEARCH: the whole Messages/Transfers tables are exported
(one row each), plus a participants roster, so a correspondent or file
transfer cannot be missed by grepping the wrong string. The db is opened
STRICTLY read-only (sqlite immutable URI — no -wal/-shm sidecars, no
locks), safe against read-only evidence mounts; an uncheckpointed -wal
sibling is surfaced as a warning.

db_path:   the store on the mounted image (e.g. .../AppData/Roaming/Skype/
           <account>/main.db). Read-only.
output_dir: CSV destination (default ./exports/chat/); must be under
           analysis/exports/reports.
chat_app:  auto | skype | whatsapp.

Read the produced CSVs with read.output. Returns _trudi_call_id for
record_finding; participants are annotated onto the trace entry so
correspondent-exhaustion checks can consume them.

tools.name: misc_device_install_inventory
tools.title: Misc Device Install Inventory
tools.description:
COMPLETE structured inventory of every device from the Windows device-install
log (setupapi.dev.log) — the BadUSB / removable-media ingress lens.

ENUMERATE, DON'T SEARCH. This parses the WHOLE log into one de-duplicated row
per physical device (class, vendor, product, VID:PID, interfaces, first/last
seen), so a keystroke injector cannot be missed by grepping the wrong string,
head-capping the dump, or windowing the wrong section. It flags the structural
keystroke-injector profile — a device exposing both HID/keyboard and mass-storage
interfaces — as a HINT on top of the full inventory; even an unflagged device is
present as a visible row for you to judge. This is the artifact a 'no BadUSB'
negative or an 'interactive human authorship' finding must be grounded on
(enforced by the broad attribution / completeness gates).

setupapi_log_path: path to setupapi.dev.log on the mounted image / triage set.
output_path: optional CSV of the FULL inventory (must be under analysis/ etc.).

tools.name: misc_cs_beacon_config
tools.title: Misc Cs Beacon Config
tools.description:
Extract Cobalt Strike beacon configs (C2, port, sleep, jitter, watermark, spawnto, UA, URIs, public-key hash) from memory dumps, a carved beacon, or a raw memory image.

path: file or directory (malfind/vadinfo/memmap dumps, raw image; scanned in
chunks, bounded by max_seconds). Finds the XOR-encoded settings block (any
single-byte key) and the runtime settings table; runtime string settings are
heap pointers, resolved from sibling vadinfo/malfind dumps or from
memmap_listing (vol windows.memmap -r json output of the process).
output_path: optional full JSON under analysis/ or exports/.
found=False with the scan inventory is a valid negative.

tools.name: misc_parse_scheduled_tasks
tools.title: Misc Parse Scheduled Tasks
tools.description:
List and read Windows Scheduled Task XML files from disk — the persistence
look an injected task lives in (no 4698 event when task-auditing is off).
tasks_dir: path to Windows/System32/Tasks/ on a mounted volume.

Windows task XML is UTF-16; it is decoded here. Each task is scanned for
keystroke-injector PAYLOAD signatures (%duck%/%bunny%/hak5, hidden/encoded
PowerShell) — flagged as a LEAD (presence flags a payload; absence supports
the benign reading). Self-logged as a citable tool_call.
